problems.title: Linked List Cycle (LeetCode 141)
problems.description: Does following next pointers ever loop back? Move one pointer one step and another two steps at a time: if they ever meet, there's a cycle.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List (LeetCode 19)
problems.description: Remove the n-th node counting from the end. Start a second pointer n steps behind the first, and watch out when the node to remove is the head.

problems.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs (LeetCode 24)
problems.description: Swap every two neighbouring nodes by rewiring their next pointers, without changing the values. Draw the arrows before and after on paper.

problems.title: Odd Even Linked List (LeetCode 328)
problems.description: Put the nodes in odd positions first, then the even ones, by keeping two chains and joining them at the end.

problems.title: Add Two Numbers (LeetCode 2)
problems.description: Two numbers are stored digit by digit in linked lists, last digit first. Walk both lists together, add with a carry, and build the answer as a new list.

exercises.title: Pointer (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Write a function that takes two pointers and changes both values: one becomes the sum, the other the absolute difference. Practises * and &.

exercises.title: Arrays Introduction (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Read numbers into an array and print them in reverse order. Try it once with indices and once by walking a pointer backwards.

exercises.title: Reverse String (LeetCode 344)
exercises.description: Reverse the characters of a vector in place: it's passed by reference, so you change the caller's vector. Swap from both ends towards the middle.

exercises.title: Print the Elements of a Linked List (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Follow the next pointers from the head and print every value, stopping at nullptr.

exercises.title: Middle of the Linked List (LeetCode 876)
exercises.description: Find the middle node. Count the nodes and walk half way, or move one pointer twice as fast as another.

exercises.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists (LeetCode 21)
exercises.description: Join two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by relinking their nodes, always taking the smaller head next.

challenges.title: Pointers & References: Basics
challenges.description: Addresses, *, & and references: change values through pointers, walk an array, and change a vector passed by reference. Do them in order.

challenges.title: Pointers & References: Linked Lists
challenges.description: Follow and rewire next pointers. Start with the three exercises (print, middle, merge), then the LeetCode problems from easiest to hardest: Linked List Cycle, Remove Nth Node From End, Swap Nodes in Pairs, Odd Even Linked List, Add Two Numbers. Draw the arrows on paper first.

quizzes.title: Pointers & References
quizzes.description: Five questions on addresses, pointers, references and passing values to functions. Answers are revealed after you submit.

questions.question: After int x{ 5 }; and int* p{ &x };, what is *p?
In int* p{ &x };, what does the & do?
answers: It gives the address of x
It makes a copy of x

questions.question: void addOne(int n) { n = n + 1; } is called as addOne(x) with x equal to 5. What is x afterwards?
Why do functions often take const std::vector<int>& v instead of std::vector<int> v?
answers: Vectors can't be passed by value
It lets the function add elements
It avoids copying the whole vector, and promises not to change it

questions.question: What happens if you use *p when p is nullptr?
answers: The program usually crashes: there's nothing at that address
p is set to a new variable automatically

lessons.title: Pointers & References
lessons.description:
How memory works, explained with houses and house numbers (about 35 minutes, after Data Types in C++): addresses, pointers and nullptr, references, passing values to functions by value, by reference and by pointer, arrays and pointers, chains of pointers, and the classic pointer bugs. Every example is a complete program you can copy and run.

After the lesson, try the "Pointers & References: Basics" and "Pointers & References: Linked Lists" challenges under Practice and the "Pointers & References" quiz.
